notes: Eval 2 (banking-plugin) assertions are MISCALIBRATED. The with-skill agent correctly applied the student-generated-data exception, but assertions assumed fabricated output exists. Baseline 'wins' on this eval by false-positiving. Recommend rewriting Eval 2 assertions to test exception handling accuracy.

Eval 3 (saudi-arabia) is the strongest discriminator: with-skill scores 100% vs baseline 33%. The skill's 6-defect taxonomy, exception rules, and priority ordering all produce measurably better results.

Eval 1 (malaysia-sukuk) shows the skill makes better classification decisions (borderline labelling vs no detection) but its fix recommendations are more conservative (relabelling vs intent table), which 'fails' assertions designed for typical fabricated outputs.
With-skill runs are FASTER on average (106s vs 140s) despite slightly more tokens, likely because the structured taxonomy prevents exploratory tangents.
Both with-skill and without-skill agents correctly avoid false positives on framework tables and prompt blocks — this assertion doesn't differentiate skill value.

KEY INSIGHT: The skill's primary value is in CLASSIFICATION PRECISION (what is/isn't fabricated, exception handling) and STRUCTURED TAXONOMY (consistent 6-type framework), not just in knowing about intent tables.
